newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to destroy half its anti-personnel mines.
newsitem.headline: France to destroy half its anti-personnel mines.

text.p: France, which recently said it would limit its use of anti-personnel landmines, said on Thursday it would destroy half its existing stock of the arms which kill or maim one person in the world every 20 minutes.
A senior defence ministry official who asked not to be identified told reporters the destruction of half the French stock would be completed by the end of next year.
He declined to say how many mines were involved.
Paris announced earlier this month that it would give up the use of anti-personnel landmines except in cases described as of "absolute necessity for the security of our forces."
French troops last used anti-personnel mines to protect their positions when they were under attack by Moslem fundamentalist guerrillas in Lebanon in 1983.

France, a major arms trading nation, said in 1993 that it would no longer export anti-personnel landmines and added last year that it would halt the production of such weapons which are meeting increasing international opposition.
The French ban does not affect anti-tank mines which are relatively less dangerous for civilians.
Between 80 millon and 110 million active landmines remain strewn around the world, often in areas where fighting has ended years earlier.
